title: Robotic Platforms for Green Vehicle Refueling and Charging Stations: A Critical Review of Fixed, Mobile, Humanoid, and Legged Solutions
content: The automation of vehicle refueling and charging stations is an emerging enabler of sustainable transportation, but the robotic platforms able to perform this task remain fragmented across disconnected research communities. This review examines two evidence-based platform families - fixed and mobile manipulator arms - and two emerging candidate families - humanoid and quadruped robots, retained as future research directions - across four refueling modalities: EV conductive charging, EV wireless charging, hydrogen refueling, and battery swapping. A PRISMA-inspired, criterion-driven search retained 84 primary sources from an initial pool of 194 records. Quantitative evidence is reported wherever available: docking success rates of 90--100\%, positional accuracy of 2-10 mm, cycle times from tens of seconds to a few minutes, and Technology Readiness Levels. Every comparative table entry carries an explicit Evidence Class (A-C), separating evidence-based findings from the extrapolation required for humanoid- and quadruped-based refueling, for which no direct study exists. Dedicated analyses address hydrogen functional safety and industrial battery-swapping architectures (NIO, CATL, Ample, Gogoro). Six technological and normative gaps, including cybersecurity, feed a five-direction, priority-ranked research roadmap. This review offers the first cross-platform, evidence-graded comparative framework in this domain, making explicit where current knowledge ends and extrapolation begins.
